sentences.text:
Chandra Shekar Gudipati vs Through The Sho on 1 October,
2019
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao

Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6030 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.154 of 2019 of Lalapet Police Station, Guntur Urban, registered for the offences under Sections 270, 273 and 284 of IPC and Sections 57(1) and 58 of Food Safety Standard Act, 2006 (for short, 'FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 19.04.2019, when the complainant along with his staff proceeded to Balaji Traders, Hajari Vaari Veedhi, Opposite to Fish Market, found the banned tobacco products in the petitioner's shop and hence, seized the same and registered a case in Crime No.154 of 2019 of Lalapet Police Station, for the offences stated supra.
3.

Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused under Sections 270, 273 and 284 of IPC and Sections 57(1) and 58 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J 01.10.2019 SS Chandra Shekar Gudipati vs Through The Sho on 1 October, 2019
